items.title: Dead/duplicate handler modules: AuthHandler & BuildingHandler unused, routes reimplement inline
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/handlers/auth/mod.rs:217 — `pub struct AuthHandler;` (login/refresh_token/register/reset_password/etc) is declared via `pub mod auth;` but has ZERO references anywhere outside its own file (verified: grep `AuthHandler` excluding handlers/auth/ = empty)
backend/servers/api-server/src/handlers/buildings/mod.rs:326 — `pub struct BuildingHandler;` (create_building/get_building/assign_owner/etc) likewise has ZERO references outside its own file

the live /api/v1/auth/* and /api/v1/buildings/* routes reimplement this logic inline in routes/auth.rs (login at routes/auth.rs:468) and routes/buildings.rs — two parallel implementations means a security/correctness fix to the route version won't propagate to the handler version, and reviewers can be misled about which path is live

modules are still declared (`pub mod auth; pub mod buildings;` in handlers/mod.rs:9-10) so the dead code compiles and is discoverable — reachability gate not triggered (mod declarations exist); flagged as refactor, not phantom-TODO

found by rotating expert review (api-handlers segment, rust+security lenses); the handler code itself is clean (signature-verified refresh, token rotation, rate limiting, org-membership + RLS scoping) — the issue is the dead duplication, not a bug inside it

resolved: code patterns no longer present in cited files — PR #437 (merged 2026-05-23) deleted handlers/auth/mod.rs, handlers/buildings/mod.rs and handlers/mod.rs (2495 net lines), removing `pub mod handlers` from lib.rs/main.rs; the handlers/ dir is gone

evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/inquiries.rs:554 — mark_as_read binds `_principal: RequestPrincipal` but discards it, calling mark_inquiry_read(id) with only the path id
wired at inquiries.rs:66 — PUT /api/v1/inquiries/{id}/read -> mark_as_read (reachable production route)
backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal.rs:768 — `UPDATE listing_inquiries SET status = 'read', read_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1 AND read_at IS NULL` has no realtor/owner predicate
sibling handlers scope correctly: get_inquiry uses get_inquiry_for_realtor(id, principal.user_id) and respond_to_inquiry(id, ...) — mark_as_read is the lone unscoped write

any authenticated portal user can flip another realtor's inquiry to read by enumerating the UUID (cross-account write IDOR); not covered by open PR #435, which defers a separate community-routes IDOR cluster

items.title: SSRF: signed-document fetch + webhook-test POST issue outbound requests to unvalidated user-controlled URLs
evidence: issue #439 (P1-05, severity high) — post-merge review of PR #435: the P1-05 fix hardened MIME/size/magic-bytes on the response body but did NOT validate signed_url itself; SSRF still open

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/signatures.rs:628 — store_signed_document does `client.get(signed_url)` on a bare reqwest::Client::new() with no host validation and no redirect policy; the comment at lines 613-619 claims SSRF hardening but only covers the response

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations.rs:2743 — webhook-test handler does `client.post(&subscription.url)` with the stored URL; redirects are disabled (Policy::none()) but the host is never checked against private/loopback/link-local ranges

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:152 — a working validate_external_url guard (is_blocked_v4 at :212) already exists but is a private method applied only at :251; verified both other sinks unguarded
authenticated org member (or a poisoned e-signature provider) can target 169.254.169.254 / 127.0.0.1 / internal services and have the server fetch/POST to them

items.title: Latent fail-open: ProtectedRoute role check is skipped when user.role is falsy
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx:117 — `if (requiredRoles && requiredRoles.length > 0 && user?.role)` short-circuits the role check when user.role is falsy, falling through to `return <>{children}</>` (fail-open)
frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx — AuthContext does not populate a `role` field on the user, so user.role is undefined in practice

no route in the app currently passes `requiredRoles` (grep of frontend/apps/ppt-web/src shows only ProtectedRoute's own definition + JSDoc) — so the bypass is LATENT, not currently exploitable; client-side gating is UX, the real authz is server-side RLS

hardening item: when role-gating goes live (relevant to the 79-2 auth-flow wiring in draft PR #444), this guard must deny on missing role rather than skip — both Frontend and Completeness reviewers independently flagged the same fall-through

items.title: Announcer: untracked clear-then-set timeouts can resurrect a stale screen-reader message
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/Announcer.tsx:49,58 — the 'clear-then-set' announce timeouts (setTimeout(() => setPoliteMessage(message), 100) and the assertive equivalent) are not stored in politeTimeoutRef/assertiveTimeoutRef; only the 3000ms clear timeout is tracked
on a rapid second announce(), the prior pending set is never cancelled, so a stale message can be written after the new one; unmount cleanup clears only the 3000ms ref, not these pending sets
low-severity a11y bug — affects screen-reader announcements only; fix is to store and clear the set-timeouts alongside the existing clear-timeout refs
